Resource limits for untrusted tokens

Source: R/limits.R
jose_limits.Rd

Every function that reads a token checks it against these limits before decoding anything, so a hostile token cannot make zujose allocate or compute much more than an honest one would. The defaults are far above what real tokens need.

Usage

jose_limits(
  token = 2^20,
  header = 2^14,
  payload = 2^20,
  signatures = 16,
  recipients = 16,
  keys = 16,
  p2c = 6e+05
)

Arguments

token

Maximum length of a token, in bytes.

header

Maximum length of a decoded protected header, in bytes.

payload

Maximum length of a payload or ciphertext, in bytes. This applies to detached and unencoded (b64: false) payloads too.

signatures

Maximum number of signatures in a JWS JSON serialization.

recipients

Maximum number of recipients in a JWE JSON serialization.

keys

Maximum number of keys tried for one token.

p2c

Maximum PBES2 iteration count a token may ask for.

Value

A list of class jose_limits.

Details

A token over a limit fails with zujose_parse_error. Use Inf to switch a limit off.

Examples

jose_limits()
#> <jose_limits>
#>   token      1,048,576
#>   header     16,384
#>   payload    1,048,576
#>   signatures 16
#>   recipients 16
#>   keys       16
#>   p2c        600,000
jose_limits(token = 8192, signatures = 1)
#> <jose_limits>
#>   token      8,192
#>   header     16,384
#>   payload    1,048,576
#>   signatures 1
#>   recipients 16
#>   keys       16
#>   p2c        600,000
